title: Meridian run human-control record
description: The complete schema for the human-control state of ONE execution run (record_type: run-human-control): a portable, storage-independent record of who is assigned which universal role, who acts now, who holds the permanent human-in-command posture, the switchable supervision mode, the communication mode, an optional independent-review requirement, and the ORDERED HISTORY of changes to every mutable control axis. It declares THIS schema in its $schema and composes the reused scoped-record.schema.json envelope with a specialised body, so a consumer that follows the declaration validates the whole record in one pass; scripts/lib/role-and-human-control.mjs additionally validates every record against scoped-record.schema.json directly, so the canonical envelope check is reused and separately performed. The record lives ONLY in scope.type run-state (scope.id identifies the run, scope.workspace_id is mandatory); project-workspace, repository-scope, built-in-methodology, user-profile and organization-profile are rejected, and origin.kind built-in is rejected. It references EXACTLY ONE execution run by a portable execution_run_ref and never embeds run state that belongs to execution-state-model — no lifecycle_stage, work_status, blockers, next step or run transition history. The independent axes: human_authority.posture is the constant human-in-command — the permanent basis, never a switchable mode and never disabled — and human_authority.holder names the participant who holds it, who MUST be assigned the owner role. supervision_mode is the closed switchable pool human-in-the-loop | human-on-the-loop; human-in-the-loop requires an hitl block (a concrete required_human_action and a declared gate) and FORBIDS an hotl block; human-on-the-loop requires an hotl block (non-empty autonomy_bounds and a stated intervention capability) and FORBIDS an hitl block; full removal of human authority is not representable. role_assignments is a non-empty list of { actor, roles } where roles is drawn from the closed pool owner, operator, executor, reviewer, verifier, git_integrator, deployer; one actor may hold several roles; an empty roles list, a blank actor, a duplicate actor and a duplicate (actor, role) pair are rejected. acting_actor names the participant acting now and MUST be one of the assigned actors. review_independence is optional: the base owner-plus-one-executor model needs no reviewer; when required is true, both reviewer_actor and reviewed_actor must be named, must differ, and the reviewer must be a separate participant assigned a reviewing role; when required is false, neither reference may be present; any reference that IS present is checked for portability whatever the value of required. communication_mode is the closed pool owner_relayed | direct, modelled separately from role and supervision. switch_history is ordered by a strictly increasing sequence; its first record states the initial establishment (from_supervision_mode, from_communication_mode, from_acting_actor and from_role_assignments are all null); every later record continues the previous record on EACH mutable axis with no break; every record states a reason (its basis) and a checkpoint_ref (the verifiable checkpoint a change preserves); every record's to_acting_actor is one of its own to_role_assignments; and the LAST record matches the whole current control state — supervision_mode, communication_mode, acting_actor AND role_assignments — not only the supervision mode. A change of mode, role, actor or communication never opens a new run. Every reference and prose string is portable. The contract is a mandatory part of the Kernel: an absent schema or absent fixtures is a validator FAIL, not an informational skip. The normative document is standards/workspace/role-and-human-control.md.

scope_ref.description: A run's human-control area. Only run-state is accepted; every other area is rejected here and in scripts/lib/role-and-human-control.mjs with the rationale. scope.id identifies the run; workspace_id ties it to the project workspace (workspace-scope-model.md §1).

origin.description: Same contract as scoped-record.schema.json's origin. A run's control state is established in a workspace, so kind 'built-in' is additionally rejected by scripts/lib/role-and-human-control.mjs.

human_authority.description: The human command posture and the participant who holds it. posture is the constant human-in-command: the owner sets the goal, the bounds of authority and the acceptable risk. It is not a member of supervision_mode and cannot be switched off. holder is a portable reference to the participant who holds it; that participant MUST be assigned the owner role in role_assignments (checked in scripts/lib/role-and-human-control.mjs).

hitl.description: Required when supervision_mode is human-in-the-loop and FORBIDDEN otherwise: a declared gate cannot be passed without an explicit human action, named here as a concrete action and the gate it stands before.

hotl.description: Required when supervision_mode is human-on-the-loop and FORBIDDEN otherwise: bounded autonomous execution runs only inside pre-set bounds and with a standing intervention capability.

role_assignment.description: One participant and the roles they hold. actor is a portable opaque participant reference. roles is a non-empty subset of the closed pool; one actor may hold several roles. A blank actor, an empty roles list, a duplicate actor and a duplicate (actor, role) pair are rejected (the last two in scripts/lib/role-and-human-control.mjs).

review_independence.description: Optional. The base owner-plus-one-executor model needs no reviewer. When required is true, reviewer_actor and reviewed_actor must both be named, must differ, and reviewer_actor must be a separate participant assigned a reviewing role. When required is false, neither reference may be present. Any reference that IS present is checked for portability regardless of required.

control_switch.description: One entry in the ordered history of control changes. sequence is the explicit ordinal (strictly increasing, never repeated or decreasing). The first entry states the initial establishment: from_supervision_mode, from_communication_mode, from_acting_actor and from_role_assignments are all null. Every later entry continues the previous entry on EACH mutable axis with no break — from_X equals the previous entry's to_X for supervision mode, communication mode, acting actor and the whole role-assignment set. to_role_assignments is a full, valid assignment set; to_acting_actor is one of its actors. reason is the mandatory basis. checkpoint_ref is the verifiable checkpoint the change preserves — a change of mode, role, actor or communication never opens a new run and never drops the run's verifiable state.

payload.description: The independent axes of one run's human-control state, as a CLOSED object. human_authority (permanent HIC plus its holder), supervision_mode (switchable HITL/HOTL), acting_actor, role_assignments, communication_mode and switch_history are separate axes and none is derived from another. hitl is required when supervision_mode is human-in-the-loop and forbidden otherwise; hotl is required when it is human-on-the-loop and forbidden otherwise.
